parts.name: preparation
parts.title: Preparation
parts.text:
1. PREPARATION
Run `vw visuals prepare` once the first cut is approved (nothing is made or paid). It writes the package under work/visuals/, one file per section (prompt.md, gaps.json, intended-visuals.json, brief.json, world-1.json and on with 25 clips each, schema.json, generators.json), and the image prompt library per step under work/visuals/library/ (section 6, in part-later.md); read a file whole, never by line offsets. Read prompt.md, gaps.json and intended-visuals.json first, and claims.json (the figures the narration rests on, and whether the operator had them checked: a picture or graphic shows the same figure, and a checked one is not searched again), the world files when you plan the scenes. Tell the operator (never ask) its one line on the footage's look, measured from the clips; their correction (the page, or `vw visuals footage`) wins. Then settle and record the treatment (section 2, part-treatment.md), before any plan or picture.

parts.name: treatment
parts.title: Treatment
parts.text:
2. TREATMENT
`direction` comes first (refused without), the central creative choice: a few lines (at most 2000 characters) on what the audience should understand or feel by the end, the storytelling viewpoint, the principal visual approach and why, and the roles of footage, stills, generated scenes and graphics; foundation.treatment starts with it word for word unless the operator approves a new treatment. A palette or "documentary mix" alone is not a direction. Choose the picture from the film's purpose, audience and script before you think about how it is made: the effort, cost or convenience of a route never chooses the medium. In a documentary or a client story, people, purposeful work and the material changing under their hands carry the film; a realistic representative scene is a legitimate picture when the footage lacks one, provided it does not pretend to be the client's own site, people or measured result. There is no quota of AI video, footage or graphics: a technical record may lean on graphics, a human story on scenes; say in the direction which the film is and why. With no footage, the direction also holds the film's one look (colours, contrast, light), approved once, read wherever a plan rule reads the footage beside a gap.
Read the whole first cut, including the retained footage before, between and after the gaps. Plan the missing passages in film order as one progression: what the audience already knows, what each adds, changes of pace, recurring visual ideas, how each enters from and exits into the neighbouring real pictures. Use a diagram, chart or illustrated graphic when the meaning is invisible to a camera or must be read precisely: the inside of something (a cross-section, a cavity, a hidden layer); a flow, force, heat or load path; a number, comparison or proportion the narration rests on; a sequence where the order matters; scale; or before and after. Use a scene (footage, or AI video or still of people and places) for people, places, materials, textures, effort, feeling and results, anything a camera could have filmed with more time. Build the film's graphics as one visual language: one recurring diagram that develops across the film reads better than many unrelated drawings. Vary the pictures: mix the shots of a gap longer than one shot (footage, an AI scene, a labelled scene, a graphic); two graphics in a row only when each passes the test above, the second's `warning_answers` saying why (warned, as is a gap of graphics only). A footage clip, or a specific thing the footage shows (one building, one machine), is named at one gap only; a second gap that wants it says why in its line, or takes another. Treat the team's intended visuals (the script's visual notes per scene, in the package) as a stated requirement with its source: follow them where they fit the direction and the footage; say in the treatment why you depart from one. The gap that opens the film (if one does) opens on the subject at work, framed wide enough to see where (the mason laying bricks on the half-built wall, the site around), never an empty view of the place; a close-up comes after a wider view. Propose in the treatment the look of a gap with no real footage beside it (palette, contrast, saturation, muted and true to life by default, light; with no footage, the direction's look), approved with it.
The treatment, in out/visual-treatment.json, has one entry per gap: `gap_id`; the words under it; the team's intended visuals, cited or departed from with the reason; `picture` in one line; `routes`; `seconds`, one number, the gap's total (a video gap's segments carry theirs inside `shots`, never a list in `seconds`); `images`, a whole number for the gap (a count, never a list: one still per AI video shot); an AI video shot is one action, at most four people, nobody crossing, hand work close and in the right hand, every transfer named and close; a picture that needs more is re-staged, or is footage, a still or a drawn shot; a line that rests on a rule on trial says so; `depicts`, one line per graphic, approved before anything is drawn; `frozen_seconds` held still (usually 0); and, for more than one route, `shots` with each `route` and `seconds`. End with your reasons; the server refuses a gap missing or twice or a field out of form, and adds per route the counts and seconds, the cost against the cap and the frozen share against its 10 % limit.
Send the draft (`vw visuals treatment --file out/visual-treatment.json`); then `vw visuals next`: the server hands the operator every line on one card, the Direction first, and you record the card with `vw visuals card` (section E; one line at a time with `vw visuals decide` where the card cannot be shown). There is no yes to the whole. Revise only a line sent back and send the draft again; unchanged accepted lines stay accepted, one your revision changed (a shared route, the totals) returns to "to accept". Recorded when every line is accepted, the treatment comes before any plan or picture; the plan is checked against it. Settle the direction in conversation before planning, and a material change as a decision before shots; never quietly rewrite an accepted foundation: a changed direction revises the treatment, sequence, affected world rules and scenes together, never a new rule beside shots that contradict it.

parts.name: plan
parts.title: The detailed plan
parts.text:
3. THE DETAILED PLAN
Order of work, in three steps, to the recorded treatment: foundation, elements, gaps (scenes, shots, states for animation shots, beats). You write the shared parts in out/plan-base.json: foundation, elements (the film's techniques among them, kind technique, named once here from the treatment and the footage; a beat verb outside them is warned, never refused), graphic style, sequence_overview, `gaps` (in order); then the missing facts (section A), their answers written into plan-base.json. Then helpers (the `vw-plan-gaps` helper, a few gaps each; start with three or four) write the gaps at once from out/plan-base.json, the package, the recorded treatment and their neighbours (pictures before and after, the people's last state), never another helper's gaps, one file each in out/plan-gaps/ (a gap, or {"gaps": [...]}), things not among the elements in `new_elements` (id and name), never invented; a short film you may write alone. `vw visuals plan-join --base out/plan-base.json --gaps out/plan-gaps/` writes out/visual-plan.json (film order, new things merged by name; a missing or doubled gap is refused; it names the new things still to complete). When a helper's report does not arrive, its file under out/plan-gaps/ (read by its full path) is the proof it finished: never relaunch a helper whose file exists. `vw visuals check --file out/visual-plan.json` until valid (it lists every item's first failure together) (it checks across gaps and prints routes, graphic seconds, images and cost against the cap); fix what it names in the gap file (its helper for a judgement, you for a field or a spelling), join again, check again; out/visual-plan.json is never edited by hand (the join refuses to overwrite one that was; `--rebuild` drops the edits). Answer each warning in the shot's `warning_answers` ({kind, answer}), never in the purpose, or change the plan; tell the operator the page's plain warnings, never the technical ones. Before proposing, review each passage's meaning and treatment fit, every subject's beats, layout and scale against the landmarks, identity against the references, continuity with the neighbours and across shots, every shot's route and length against its generator, every sequence's states, and exact placement timing. `vw visuals propose --file out/visual-plan.json` (refused before the recorded treatment, when a gap's route departs from it, or when foundation.treatment does not start with the direction); `vw visuals select --gap G --choice C` for an offered choice; then `vw visuals next`: the server asks an offered choice first, as buttons, then hands the operator the gaps on one card, and you record the card with `vw visuals card` (section E; one gap at a time with `vw visuals decide` where the card cannot be shown); never `accept --gaps all`. A plan proposed again keeps every acceptance it did not touch. When the new version changes only the part every gap shares (the foundation, the sequence rules), the server asks the operator ONE question for all the gaps whose own shots are unchanged, and lists what changed; a gap whose own shots changed is asked by itself, with what changed. Never ask those gaps one by one, never say yourself what changed or that a gap is unchanged: show what the server hands out. Change the foundation or a sequence rule only when the change asked for needs it, and say so before you propose. Before any picture, read every gap's words in `vw visuals status`: a change asked for, or a gap sent back, is a revision (Revise, or `vw visuals revise --gap G --notes "…" --quote "…"`): revise its treatment entry and plan (one helper for one gap), propose again for fresh acceptance and generate nothing for it until then; unchanged gaps stay accepted.
The foundation, a practical casting and production-design brief, has one topic per rule (id, statement, scope, source) in separate categories: world (place, period, people and their work, wardrobe, environment, materials, tools, signage, language, the process; short positive statements, only what this film needs, no invented region or dress); exclusions (detectable consequences of the direction, each naming the decision it protects; no generic negatives, no ban on a medium because one option was rejected); specifications; production_constraints (narration and first cut preserved); editing_constraints (rejected pictures, their intervals); appearance (style, colour, lighting; texture, sharp or soft, from the measured footage character, the operator's correction winning; with no footage, the direction's look). Layouts live in scenes, identities in elements, temporal rules in sequence_rules; the foundation alone should let another director work. Each statement is one of three kinds: a requirement or observed fact with its source (brief, script, the operator's words, a clip finding), applied no wider than the evidence; a creative choice marked Proposed, with its film-specific reason; a consequential unknown, asked in open_questions and `vw visuals ask`, when a choice would assert real geography, identity, culture or performance the sources do not establish. Never fill an unknown with a stereotype or an inferred nationality, nor defer every casting and environment decision: propose the shared direction now, defer exact identities and props. sequence_overview first: what each gap adds to the treatment's progression. An ordinary gap has one proposal in gap.scenes (treatment_fit: its part in the sequence); two choices (each with scenes, a recommended_choice, a plain decision_reason; other shapes refused) only for a real ambiguity, a production constraint or the operator's request. A plain or studio background only when the treatment allows it (`studio_background`, with the reason); objects shown where made, kept or used, not alone.
Meaning. Give each passage its key meaning, emotional weight and a concrete method (evidence, process, a person's experience, or another justified approach). An abstract thought, feeling or statistic is valid narration: never rewrite it for a camera or fabricate documentary evidence (a graphic may explain a statistic); never invent facts, people, claims, scale or physical mechanisms. Per shot: `claims` and `descriptors`, never shown as their opposite (warned when missing on a shot with narration); `evidence` when it carries a claim (a test, a table, or the result in a scene, never an unrelated picture; warned when missing); `claim`, visible (footage first; warned on a graphic) or invisible; `fact_ids` into `visual_facts` (how a material, process or setting really looks and is done; source and status: confirmed, observed, unknown; warned when missing on a shot of a material or process); `carries_over` for a process's next step (one process, one place, light and crew; "on top of that" or "once" is no process); `message`, with `adds` (a number, a cause, a consequence) when it repeats, or the two become one shot. An MCU, CU or ECU resting on an unknown fact is refused: frame wider or ask the operator.
Elements. Derive them from the planned shots (secondary subjects, named background workers, props), each exact (the same individual, object or place throughout) or representative, with its views. Anything specific to the client the footage shows (a wall pattern, a product, a tool, a uniform) is its own exact object element, its footage frames as views and its description once in the world rules as exact text; until its golden picture exists, its pictures send one of those frames as a parent, never words alone. A thing whose fact or size cites the footage (a clip or its frame; a maker's "door frame" is not footage) is `identity: exact` with an approved footage frame before any picture, measured first (`vw visuals measure`, status measured) when its size is unknown: warned in the plan, refused at the picture. Materials and processes the film relies on are elements (kind material, process), as are tools in a holding or props list (object) and techniques a beat names as its working action (technique: pointing, plastering, welding; not a gesture or a tool's name: "points at the crack", "picks up the drill"), all in the reference round; a technique is `identity: representative` (the trade's usual way) unless its fact or size cites the footage (the client's own technique, as filmed): then `identity: exact` with an approved footage frame, like any thing the footage shows; a missing technique is refused (`status.needed_elements`). Every person, object and animal has its real `size` (client material, `measure` on footage frames, a maker's sheet; else unknown, never invented; warned when missing; a generic, standardised thing's size may be proposed from a named standard or maker figure, status `proposed`, source "recalled: <standard>, to confirm", put to the operator in the missing-facts list beside its alternatives and the footage measure, and recorded on their word as confirmed, source "the operator confirmed <standard>": it may shape the drawing, never a number written on screen (that needs the script, the client's document or a web check); a client's own thing is never proposed from recall), a material its sizes in its `material_spec`; a claim in `claims` about the subject's own size, amount or scale is refused without a size value and `compare_to` (another element in frame); a size word in `descriptors` or a beat describes and is not checked, except on a graphic or drawn shot or for light, less, fewer or short not about size. Refused without: a person's `description`, its fixed layer; each scene's `outfit` per person shown (garments and colours only, identical for a person across scenes; a framing note goes in the shot's `focus`, a question in `open_questions`); `time_jump` (the script's words) when a garment or a colour changes. Two people in one film wear different colour families unless the footage or the brief fixes their clothes (a uniform). Nothing in the frame vanishes: everything in the shot at its start is accounted for at its end, still there at a stated place (a subject's `end`, a prop's end) or gone by a stated action of someone; anything that moves or is moved is a named subject or prop of the shot, the container that brings a thing included (warned as container_unnamed). A real person required speaking on camera is the real person: `speaker: true`, every shot of them footage (`visual_type: footage`), other angles (listening, hands at work, profile, from behind) only from their own footage; AI pictures or takes of them are refused.
Scenes and life. A scene is one setting, time and purpose; beats are the smallest visible actions. `activity_level` (quiet, normal or busy) from the narration and the brief; a normal or busy scene shows the implied life (who else does what) and the working equipment (warned). Up to three background people are named workers (elements with beats; a sheet only with a source picture); more are a crowd: the ambient line plus one `groups` entry, `mode: varied`, a count and at least 2 traits used in turn; more than 3 named in a scene are refused; a passer-by without beats lives only in each scene's words, different each time (warned as an element). Everything visible that acts (person, animal or object) has beats; a still one holds, with `hold_reason`, unchanged; in a video shot a living holder moves a body-length by the end unless `hold_reason` names small life (breathing, chewing, the head, the hands, the tail, the ears) and it is not standing in a normal or busy scene (refused otherwise). A scene with a video shot has its ambient line: one line on what moves around the action (leaves in the breeze, dust or smoke in the air, people at work behind), from the setting and the neighbouring footage, or 'still' (warned without; the server writes it into every take and the take check asks for it); every scene its `light` once (a scene of graphics only (diagrams, sequences, drawn) has none; the sources against the landmarks, the main one, hard or soft, colour, strength; warned without; the check measures each picture's light and colour against the footage beside it and marks a large jump) and its air (dust, smoke, haze, steam or clean), matched to the footage beside the gap (with no footage, the direction's look) and named word for word in the prompt (soft overcast light, muted greens). Props fit the work and the region (a tea glass on a site), never what the setting forbids (no smoking, flame or spark near fuel, gas or chemicals) or an unsafe practice shown as right. Work leaves traces (tools, offcuts, mortar droppings, footprints; signs of use in a finished house): a place shown needs `signs_of_use` (two or more, each at one of its landmarks; refused without) unless the treatment approves it clean (a show home at handover, a new empty room, a showroom), the reason in `staged_clean`. In a video shot, several of a kind in one frame (counted above one, or a framing word such as workers, people, cows, unless negated: "no workers yet") need a `groups` entry, `same` (with the reason), `different` (one trait per head) or `varied` (at least 2 traits; refused otherwise).
Positions, states and beats. Lay out each scene with named landmarks (the doorway, the table, the near wall), room positions apart from the screen sides; a moving subject heads for something in frame or coming into view. Each subject: a role, screen position, start and end states, facing, pose, held objects and progress; an acting one ordered timed beats (start and end, target, path, contact, visible result). Its first beat starts exactly in the subject's `start` state and its last beat ends exactly in its `end` state, field for field (position, facing, pose, holding, progress, objects, gaze), and each beat starts in the previous beat's end (refused otherwise, naming the shot, the subject, the beat and the fields that differ). Refused: a position without landmark, `amount` and `unit`; `facing` not a heading; `objects` without `count` and `place`; a held tool without `props`; an object count that changes without its `changes` entry; a carriable thing in `fixed`; a beat without `done` or with a free-word target (a landmark or an element id of the shot; describe it in path and result); a person's state without `gaze` (its target may be `camera`) unless `face_in_frame` is false; a video shot whose `fixed` is not three landmark ids (all when fewer; at MCU, CU or ECU only those in frame, none allowed); a beat shorter than its `min_s` (one brick, about 3 s) or actions that overrun the shot. Warned: a missing `min_s`; a look as the only change (prefer a profile or a back view); an acting video shot without `changes` (none for ambient-only shots); a state changed between shots without a note (a cut never teleports a person or resets work). The server writes the rule lines from these fields (two signs of use per shot, or 'clean and unused, as planned') and checks every picture and take against them; `status.figure_repeats` names repeated background figures. `boundary_continuity` (required): how the first and last shot continue the neighbours on both sides, footage or planned (at the film's start or end, the one side).
Timing and movement. Narration is timed per gap (gaps.json `timing`: sentences in seconds, words in frames; context.timing adds the sentences either side). Cut in a pause, never inside a word; a shot's `narration` is the words it covers, its picture starting on or just before them, a title or label on its word (warned otherwise). Shots run two to eight seconds as a rule, never mechanically equal; AI video 1 to 15 s on screen (a take is made at 3 s or more and trimmed; under 1 s use a picture; over 15 s refused; an action of 9 s or more is better as two shots cut on the action); a picture or a drawing may be a second or two. Real footage in a gap is a footage shot (`visual_type: footage`, `vw visuals clip`), under the timing, crop, reuse and no-repeat rules only, not those for generated pictures (the 15 s limit and `information_progression` among them). Every still and graphic state moves 5 % (`motion`, from the composition); a graphic or a text picture only push_in or none; `none` needs `motion_reason` (refused otherwise). Warned: a moving still over 4 s, a frozen one over 3 s, a graphic state over 5 s, one graphic over 4 s (not a title or text card: a build of 2 to 4 states or a drawn animation), a label or one number under three seconds, a run of graphics over 8 s (a building diagram fits within; break it with a camera shot). Fill a longer stretch with several stills, a clip stretch (`vw visuals clip --shot S --clip C --at <in seconds>`) or a take. Each shot has a size (EWS, WS, MWS, MS, MCU, CU, ECU) and a camera_reason (eye level honest, low powerful, high vulnerable, a slow push draws in; no angle has one fixed meaning; warned when missing, footage excepted). Warned unless size_reason states a reveal: a scene opening closer than MWS, three shots in a row at one size, a close-up (MCU or closer) of a subject not yet seen wider (`continues_footage: true` on a scene counts the footage beside the gap as that view). A clip needing more than 1.35× to fill the frame keeps bars (warned): crop it to the frame's shape (`vw visuals clip … --crop x,y,w,h`) or choose another. Name every join: `transition_in` on every shot (`transition_out` on a gap's last shot only): cut, dissolve or match; a dissolve or a match with `transition_reason`; refused without. No picture shows twice: a clip on screen (first cut or here) is a reuse, a frozen frame of a clip playing elsewhere never shows, no two shots share a start image or still. A return to a subject is a reimagined shot (`return_of`, `differs_by`; refused without), the earlier picture only as identity reference. A plain reuse only when that adds nothing: `vw visuals clip|still … --reuse "<reason>" --considered "<the reimagined shot and why it adds nothing>" --crop x,y,w,h`, refused under 60 s from the other showing, on the same stretch or beyond the clip's safe enlargement, then held for the operator's words (the page, or `vw visuals reuse --shot S --quote "<their words>"`); warned: the frozen share, pictures that look alike.
Graphics. A graphic that builds or reveals is one animation shot of two to four states, each adding something and holding at least three seconds, together filling the shot (refused otherwise); an unchanging one is a diagram shot, one still. A drawn shot is named at plan time by `visual_type: drawn` alone (no `scene_svg` yet); its scene is drawn, uploaded and named after the picture search (section 9, in part-later.md). `graphic_kind`: `diagram`, `chart`, `map`, `title` or `text` (a card checked only for its words, spelling and size). Each state names the claims and words it shows (`what_appears`, `words`; what none names is checked on the last) and starts on its `words`. `depicts`: the film's subject in its own form; an alternative (the conventional way, a competitor's) only as a labelled contrast the narration calls for. Labels: short complete phrases ("25 % fewer bricks", not "↓ 25 %"), numbers with units, leader lines ending on their part, at least 4 % of the frame height (titles 6 %), readable on a phone, in the answer's exact text (section B). Each claim spoken over a graphic is in `claims` (a must line) or `claims_left_out` with the reason; a build has a state per claim (warned); a state like the one before is refused; the assembly film is checked for every planned state. One graphic style per film (foundation.graphic_style: palette from the client card, line weight, labels, background, frame fill), made first as a style sheet (`vw visuals image --element _STYLE --kind style --answer …`), approved, in the --parents of every graphic's first (or only) picture, later states inheriting it; every picture and take carries its --answer; warned: missing claims, depicts, style, spec approval or answers.
Drawing specs. A drawing of a real object has a `drawing_spec` (warned without; an idea graphic with no real object or figure, such as heat leaving a house, needs none): parts, relationships, each size with status (confirmed: the client's source; measured; unknown) and source, and `view` with `view_reason` (refused without; a section defaults to cutaway), checked on the drawing. Research every size before the spec is shown, in this order: the client's material; the footage, measured (`vw visuals measure --refs F1 F2 --question "<what to measure>"` on approved footage frames, each number keeping its clip and time; paid: announce, never ask); a standard or maker's sheet on the web, with URL and figure (one warning and one yes cover every web figure of the run); an approved reference picture for a shape numbers cannot hold. Each value carries its source and status, a spec of a real object its proportions (a brick about 3 : 1.5 : 1; a drawing spec is warned without them, a material spec refused). Refused: an unknown with a value, a figure the shot's narration or claims state marked unknown (it is confirmed from the script), an illustrative drawing not labelled "illustrative, not to scale" (no numbers, no free proportions). A size may still wait for its research (paid measures and web figures come after the picture search): an `unknown` size without all four sources in `tried`, and `illustrative: true` when nothing is unknown or missing when something is, are warned in the plan (`spec_unresearched`) and refused when the spec is approved; `status.illustrative` warns above one in four. The SVG scene labels known sizes with units. The operator never types a size: they approve the run's specs in one table (`vw visuals spec` with no --shot, or the page) or send a correction (`vw visuals spec --shot S --notes "…"`, in `spec_corrections`): fold into out/visual-plan.json (`vw visuals plan`), propose again (approval refused until then); one late spec: `vw visuals spec --shot S --quote "…"`.

parts.name: picture-search
parts.title: The picture search
parts.text:
4. THE PICTURE SEARCH
The references are one round for every element at once (people, objects, places, the materials and processes the film relies on), never one element at a time. `vw visuals elements` shows where each is seen in the footage (work/visuals/elements.json); grab a frame of each the footage has (`vw visuals frame --file`, free); write out/reference-round.json, one row per element: element_id, its frame reference ids, and `prompt` (a thing: the subject block, what the picture must represent, its frame, nobody in it, never how the work is done; the server adds the kept preamble, the set line, the cosmetics from the plan and the four notes; a person: the why line); send it (`vw visuals round --file out/reference-round.json`) and run `vw visuals next` (section E). A clip frame is free and exact, source and time kept (`vw visuals frame --element E --clip <id> --at <seconds>`); search the clip analyses first, footage left out of the edit included (not the operator's explicit exclusions), and take the sharpest frame, the subject large and evenly lit, never a blurred one for identity. A footage frame of a person serves your description only, never the picture AI (a footage frame may still be a video take's start image); the server writes a person's sheet from the plan (description, outfits, place, your why line, one line against every other person) as three separate pictures: full length, working pose, the face; every worker the words act with is an element (the check warns of one missing).
`vw visuals status --wait 900` until the round is complete; ask nothing per element and generate nothing meanwhile. Step 1: each thing gets the footage picture or Ignore this; Done approves the frames and makes every set at once, silently, by the kept method: three separate pictures, one per turn of one conversation, from real photographs with Google Search and Image Search on (a thing with an approved footage picture gets no AI set: that picture is its reference and its golden picture). Step 2, when every set is back: the operator judges them all in one shot: Yes (ticking the golden picture of a thing, the one every shot starts from; a person's is the full-length front), No, or Correct it with their words; Done records all; the No and Correct it sets are made again with the words in the prompt, never from a rejected picture, and come back for another step 2. In chat: `vw visuals round --verdicts out/round-verdicts.json --quote` ({element: {verdict: approve|ignore}}), then `vw visuals round --sets out/round-sets.json --quote` ({element: {verdict: yes|no|correct, words, golden}}). Refused by name on such a film: the Google Images search, the picks, nothing-fits, the separate golden call; a round answer without `kept` is an older film's and keeps them (search keywords: two to twelve words, the thing and its place or trade): follow the tool's answers. Meanwhile, for accepted gaps only and without generating or spending, draft the answer forms of every diagram, chart and title card, the drawing and material specs (the client's material and the plan; paid measures and web figures after the round) and the drawn layouts; nothing new on the page and no question until the round closes, then the drafts' questions as one list; update drafts the round changed. The operator can add their own picture (`vw visuals supply`) or undo Done on step 1 (`vw visuals round --undo`). Then part-later.md, sections 5 and 9.

parts.name: later
parts.title: The later steps (references, sheets and golden pictures; shot pictures and videos; checks; review and record; brand)
parts.text:
5. GENERATED REFERENCES, SHEETS AND GOLDEN PICTURES
Name the shot a composed picture is for (`--shot S`): its claims, words, the state carried over and its facts are checked on the picture, with two practice lines on every scene picture (a plausible setting and scale; tools handled as a practitioner would).
- A generated reference: `vw visuals image --element E --kind isolated|sheet|keyframe --prompt "…" [--parents R1,R2]`, or several at once with `--file out/images.json`; paid, tell the operator. `--variants 2` for a start. One change per edit. An edit names each picture it sends as Image 1 to Image N, with what to take from it. A failed check marks the picture and shows its lines; a fix is made only on request: `vw visuals fix --ref R` (paid: tell the operator the line and the cost). An exact object gets one close reference. Every object or place gets one generated reference sheet from its approved footage frames and the operator's picks, its notes applied (the server adds each note of the operator under its picture and checks the sheet against it; a web picture also gets the watermark line: never repeat them); a person's sheet is made from words: look at their footage pictures and describe them (build, age, posture, garments and how they are worn, hair), and the sheet is made from that description. The golden picture (a person: the sheet), not the frames or the picks, is what shots bind. A footage or web picture of a person is never sent to the picture AI, as a parent or otherwise, nor copied: the sheet shows a representative person with that posture, dress, build and features; a real public figure kept exact only on the operator's instruction.
Every candidate is shown to the operator (`vw visuals fetch --ref R`) and approved by its exact hash with their words (`vw visuals approve --ref R --sha <sha> --quote "…"`). An approved place picture may guide an object inside it through a precise textual selector on the bind (`--selector ELEMENT=REF:"the near wooden chair"`); a selector never substitutes a person or an unrelated subject.

6. SHOT IMAGES AND VIDEO
An AI video shot is made from a guide; load the `vw:guide` skill and follow it. In order: a `vw-guide-scene` helper writes the scene description (`vw guide scene --shot S --file …`; the server refuses it before any spend and says why); the check frames (`vw guide frames`); a fresh `vw-guide-check` helper's verdict (`vw guide verdict`); the server renders the guide; the still, made on GPT image from the guide's first frame (`vw guide still`, paid); the operator approves it on its overlay (`vw guide look`, `approve`, or `repair`, or `reject`); the take's words (`vw guide prompt`). Every video shot in which a subject acts lists its `changes`, each with the beat that causes it; nothing appears, vanishes or grows without a subject doing it in the shot's seconds. A passage longer than one take is several shots, each with its own guide and still, cut where an action begins or ends, never at a round number of seconds.
The take is paid for only on the operator's word: show them the ready-to-shoot card (the guide, the still on its overlay, the words, the cost), then `vw guide shoot --shot S --quote "<their words>"`. A rejected take needs its cause before another (`vw guide cause`): the first frame against the still, then the guide, only then the words; the same request is never sent twice, and after two rejected takes from one camera the shot is cut, re-angled or left out.
A still shot needs no bind: approving the picture made for it (`image --shot S`) places it in the shot, in one step (approving places it; `vw visuals still --shot S --ref R --quote "…"` is for a footage frame or a picture approved before). A graphic sequence is approved and held in one call: `vw visuals sequence --shot S --quote "…"`; the server takes the states in order from the pictures made for the shot, each made from the one before; each state's hash is recorded. Show the operator all states together before asking. Every picture is made for its shot and is listed, checked and placed only there. A picture comes out of a shot with `vw visuals unplace --shot S --quote "…"`; one made for another shot moves only with the operator's words (`still --move "…"`); a web picture is a guide and never goes into the film.

The image prompt library is in work/visuals/library/: read always/ once, and a step's folder once before its first prompt (steps.json maps them; the packet names the step's files and fills the job form). Write each prompt in the library's VideoWizard answer form to out/answers/<id>.json, run its lint, and pass it with `--answer`. Where the library and this prompt or the server's fixed lines disagree, VW-MAP's overrides apply. When a library rule helped, failed or was missing, say so in one line as the answer's `suggestion`, naming the file and section; the library is not yours to change.

7. CHECKS AFTER A TAKE
After a take: a take at least as long as its placement matches it (assembly trims to the frames); a shorter take is reported with its shortfall and needs timing notes before it is accepted (assembly holds its last frame). No unbounded paid retries.

8. REVIEW OF A TAKE OR A SEQUENCE
A graphic sequence is reviewed as its states, in the chat: every label read, the drawing unchanged from state to state, the holds right for reading. A take as follows.
Gemini reads every ready take before the operator watches it: anything appearing or vanishing without a cause, the same tools, clothes and faces, an action repeated without its precondition, a change of shape or size, the planned end. Its marks, with their seconds, are on the take's card and in `vw visuals status`: tell the operator what was marked, then let them watch; they keep the take or ask for another, never taken again on a mark alone. Fetch each ready take (`vw visuals fetch --job J`) and let the operator watch it; a thumbnail is not a review. Say what you will check (the answer's checklist) and, after they have watched, what you saw, with the measured duration against the placement. On their yes, `vw visuals select --job J --notes … --quote …` records the review and the selection; on a no, `vw visuals review --job J --decision rejected --notes … --quote …`; a new take only when the operator asks.
Record the gaps when every shot has a selected take, a still or an asset: `vw visuals record --gaps all --quote "<their yes>"`.

9. THE LATER STEPS, IN ORDER
Then the round's sets (the kept method, part-picture-search.md): every element's set judged in the chat, one at a time (`vw visuals next`, section E; never `vw visuals round --sets` for the operator); an older film: one sheet per element from its approved frames and picks (`image --kind sheet --parents F1,W2`; a person's from your description, no picture parents). A start keyframe or a picture for a still names its shot (`--shot S`, or `shot` per row in the file) so its claims, words, the state carried over and its facts are checked. References made by the picture AI, the fourth source after the round: a generated image (never a start keyframe for a video shot: its still is made from its guide; `image --file out/images.json` for several at once, or `image --element E --kind keyframe --prompt "…"`, each with `--answer out/answers/<id>.json`, the library's answer form, or an `answer` path per item in the file; paid, the run's image model; inform, do not ask; the server refuses a call that would pass the cap). For a diagram, chart or labelled picture put every label and number in the answer's `exact_text` (text, place, size); the server writes it into the prompt; check each on the candidate before asking for approval. A state of a sequence: `image --element E --kind state --parents <previous state> --prompt "<only what changes>"`. The end image of a video shot: write its request with the start (`end_prompt`, `end_answer`, `end_region`; the prompt names only what changes); the server makes it from the start once the operator approves the start; show the end beside its start for approval. After a drift or a rejection, make the next end image from the approved start, never from a candidate; a state from the last approved state. After submitting a wave of images, write the next shot's answers (each start with its end request: one approval wave per shot) instead of waiting; `vw visuals status --wait 300` only when nothing is left to write. Show each candidate (`fetch --ref R`) and record their yes: `approve --ref R --sha <sha> --quote "…"`, several at once with `approve --file out/approvals.json` (rows of ref, sha, quote). The golden picture (a thing's approved footage picture, else the ticked picture of its set; a person's full-length front, which brings the face close-up into every shot by default) is what shots bind; a footage or web picture of a person is never sent to the picture AI. An older film: one sheet per object or place from its frames and picks (`image --kind sheet --parents F1,W2`), a person's from your words, its sheet the golden picture. An edit names each picture it sends as Image 1 to Image N, with what to take from it. A failed check marks the picture and shows its lines; a fix is made only on request: `vw visuals fix --ref R` (paid: tell the operator the line and the cost). When anything waits for the operator, give them the label and the link that `vw visuals status` prints for it (for example "Still · B01_S2" and its link), never only "on the page"; after each verdict, tell them the line the server answers with (what happens next, with the film time). In the chat a verdict is one button with no typed words: approve, Use for the shot, Remove, select a take, search, save the ticked pictures, the round's Done; a Reject's reason is optional (quick chips or a short note). In chat pass the operator's words as `--quote` when they give some. Every repeating material (kind material, or `repeating: true`: bricks, tiles, blocks, planks, pavers) carries one `material_spec` on the element (unit sizes with sources, `laid`, `joint`, `pattern`, `proportions`), made like a drawing spec from the same sources and never typed by the operator; it is shown on the References step beside the sheet and approved once (`vw visuals spec --element E`; a correction: `vw visuals spec --element E --notes`); the server pastes its sentence into every prompt that shows the material and checks the unit ratio and the pattern as a must line; no picture of the material is made before the approval; relative words (short, long, about 2:1, roughly, standard) are refused in your prompt. Every element's 'not this' list is the server's: `vw visuals not-this --element E` builds it once from the round's near misses, one model call on the spec and this film's rejections (a material's is built with its spec approval when missing; every later rejection adds its words); the server pastes it into every prompt that shows the element; a shot that needs an exception names it in `allows` and the line says so. The golden picture: as soon as an element's sheet (and its material spec) is approved, `status.golden_due` names it: write its golden picture at once, no question to the operator (`vw visuals image --element E --kind isolated --golden --parents <sheet>,<footage frame> --prompt`: the element in its real place at the shot size the plan uses most; a client's own object sends its footage frame here and never again); the operator approves it beside the sheet; a person's identity sheet is its golden picture. Every later picture of the element has the golden picture as Image 1 ("Image 1 is the [element]. Repeat it exactly; change nothing about it. The only change is: …"); a derived picture is never a parent (an end is made from its approved start; a graphic's states chain); a fix round's output is never a parent; a picture approved with a stated flaw cannot be golden. Every end image is an edit inside one region of its start (several places or the framing itself: a start-only take instead): `--region left,top,width,height` (or `--end-region` with the start, for the end the server queues; fractions of the frame, a third at most; name the landmark in the prompt); the server masks it and copies the start back outside it. On a Gemini film a region edit is also said in words (the server still copies the start back outside the region), and a component is made on chroma green, which the server keys out. Words to be read in a picture (a title, a label, a sign, a word on a bag) go only through the answer's `exact_text`, each entry {text, place: {landmark_id} or {region: 'lower third, inside the safe area'}, size_pct}; an entry with no place or size is refused, quoted words in the prompt that are not an entry are refused, and the server writes 'Render exactly this text, letter for letter, nothing else: …' and checks reads-exactly, the place and no other lettering on every picture. Up to the image model's limit of pictures go in with a prompt (16 for GPT Image; 14 for Gemini, by kind: 6 of things, 5 of people, 3 of style; the server names the excess), in this order: Image 1 the golden picture of the element the picture is for (an end image: its start; else the picture edited or the scene parent), then one identity sheet per person in frame, then every other approved frame, golden picture or supplied reference of a thing in the shot (its tool, its material, its look); each with one job line ('Image k is …: take …, nothing else'); a picture goes in only when its thing is in the shot's element_ids (the style, a person in frame and the start excepted; the server refuses the rest by name); a parent may be cropped to the thing with `--parents K1,L2@left,top,width,height` (fractions of the frame; the server crops before the upload, stores the crop beside the picture and the check reads the crop); the server adds to every prompt the known sizes of the shot's elements as numbers ('Sizes: Broom: broom length 600 mm'), the height words of the layout ('Heights: the plinth top reaches a standing person's knee …') and, for a picture of another thing sent for its look, what that picture also shows ('Image k also shows a bicycle and a clay pot: show none of them'), each such thing a must line of the check. Once an element's sources are approved the server cues its reference sheet like the golden picture (`sheet_due` in status): write it at once with every source as a parent (a person: from your description, no picture parents); the server adds the required views, each labelled, and 'the thing alone on plain ground'. For each exact object, make a scale reference: a footage frame with a hand or a person beside it; else an edit placing it beside two or three objects of the same shoot at true relative size, with no text. When a shot shows a client material at medium or closer, bind its footage frame as the texture reference of the video (the video bind only; its pictures carry it through the golden picture); in a place with a footage frame, bind that frame as the look reference (the packet's bind_advice names them).
Still shots need no bind or packet: approving the picture made for the shot places it (approving places it; `vw visuals unplace --shot S --quote "…"` takes it out); `still --shot S --ref R --quote "…"` places a footage frame or a picture approved before, or several in one call `still --file out/stills.json` (rows of shot, ref, quote). Video shots: the guide, its still and its take, by the `vw:guide` skill; the older `bind`, `packet`, start image, `prepare-take` and `take` are retired for them (the server refuses each by name). Animation shots: `sequence --shot S --quote "…"`, the states in the order they were made, shown together first. Video shots: every take is an edit of a guide, 3 to 15 s, as long as its guide; a longer passage is split into shots, cut where an action begins or ends; a take is selected with where it starts in its slot (`select --job J --in-s 0.4`; with none, the slot sits in the middle of the take). A shot under 4 s with no visible action is a moving still by default (a footage frame or an AI still with a push or a pan); AI video or a graphic build there needs its reason in its `warning_answers` (kind short_route), never in the purpose; the check warns without one; a still that carries words (`carries_text`, every graphic, a picture with exact text) moves by push_in or not at all and is placed whole, never cropped or panned (the renderer refuses a pan on it); the route counts show moving and frozen stills apart. A graphic with measurements, quantities or sequences that must be exact (any figure in its claims or spec: a number, size or count; words alone do not decide the route) takes the drawn route: `visual_type: drawn`, named so in the plan; on a motion film (the default) it is made with HyperFrames (section 11); on a `--drawn svg` film its `scene_svg` comes after the picture search, once the pictures it places are approved and its spec's sizes are researched: the scene is one SVG file (data, never code), uploaded then with `vw visuals scene --shot S --file scene.svg` (checked against the rules below on upload, refused with the reasons) and named in the plan by the sha256 the upload returns (a revision; the gap stays accepted), with `actions` (appear, build, move, highlight with its `color` (#RRGGBB, chosen per drawing to stand out against the background and everything in the frame, the brand colours where they stand out), fade; `ids` are element ids of the SVG; a `build` on a `<g>` steps through its children `every_s` apart) keyed to `at_s` or a `word` of the shot's narration; the SVG keeps to a viewBox of the film's shape (16:9 or 9:16), plain shapes, paths, text, g, use, gradients, filters, clipPath and mask, #RRGGBB colours from the approved palette, the film's font (asked once before the first drawing, Noto Sans recommended: `vw font <name> --quote`) or the run's brand font, every text at least 4 % of the frame height, at most eight words and inside the inner 90 % of the frame, no script, no style element, no animation, no external link; the things in it are pictures: `<image href="ref:<id>">` of an approved component or the golden picture (a thing is never drawn from shapes when a picture can show it), and the drawn layer adds the exact parts (labels with their units, arrows, bars, courses as `<use>` repeats); a drawing spec is required when the shot carries figures, its known sizes are written as labels with their units and an unknown size shows no figure; `vw visuals draw --shot S` (refused while the shot has no uploaded scene or its drawing spec is not approved) renders it free: the server checks the rules, measures every text, renders in Chromium, reads a contact sheet of every frame against the shot's lines with the style and the shot's pictures, corrects the SVG and renders again up to twice, then shows the drawing, its sheet and what it fixed on the Takes step; a drawing whose must lines still fail is held: `select` needs `--notes` saying why it is taken, else reject it with what to change; `vw visuals scene --shot S --download` brings the server's corrected SVG back; the film's brand font is given once with `vw visuals font --file brand.ttf`, Noto Sans otherwise. A component is the picture of one thing a drawn shot places: `vw visuals image --element E --kind component --prompt "one <thing>, front on"`, made in the approved style (the style picture is Image 1, added by the server) on a transparent background, checked for one thing alone with a clean edge and a transparent PNG, approved on the Pictures step like any picture, then reused by every scene of the run. The drawn route is for what must be exact: sizes, counts, a sequence of courses, a comparison of measured things; a diagram or build with exact sizes or numbers that is not drawn is refused; a conceptual graphic with nothing exact (an idea, icons, a mood) is a picture, a still with a push-in or a graphic sequence of states, never shapes standing for things; the usual drawn shot is the hybrid: the approved pictures placed as images, the exact parts drawn over them; AI video for graphics stays off; then `vw guide shoot` for each shot the operator says to shoot (paid; ask) and `status --wait 600` until every take is ready (one line per job; whole in work/visuals/status.json); each ready take is read by Gemini first (about ₹1–2 a take, informed): its marks are in the status line and on the take's card; tell the operator what was marked, then `fetch --job J`, let the operator watch, and on their yes `select --job J --notes "<what you checked>" --quote "…"`; on a no `review --job J --decision rejected --notes "…" --quote "…"` and prepare again only when they ask for a correction. A file the operator supplies, on their instruction only: `vw upload --stage visuals --file out/x.mp4` then `asset --shot S --file out/x.mp4 --kind movie --quote "…"`. Bind only what the shot's subjects and place need, and say why each reference is bound.
`vw visuals record --gaps all --quote "<their yes>"` records every gap whose shots are done; repeat as the rest finish. `vw next` moves on when all gaps are recorded.

10. BRAND
Brand: the brief's client card carries the palette, the brand guidelines and the competitors; generated pictures follow the palette and guidelines, never show a competitor, and never generate a logo. A card with no colours: ask the operator once which they prefer and record their words (`vw colours "<their words>" --quote`; "no preference" is an answer); a preferred colour is never forced where it would not stand out. A real logo for a reference element: `vw brand fetch` saves the directory's logo files under in/brand/, then `vw visuals supply --element E --file in/brand/<name>`.

11. DRAWN SHOTS WITH HYPERFRAMES
A film draws with HyperFrames unless started with `--drawn svg` (`scene` and `draw` are refused on a motion film); there a diagram, chart, map or timeline that carries text is a drawn shot, never a painted one. Once a drawn shot's pictures and spec are approved: `vw motion brief --shot S` for each; one `vw-motion-rules` helper per shot, all at once (it writes work/motion/S/rules.md before anything is drawn); when the brief leaves a fact open, show the operator rules.md and ask them to tick, strike or add, once. Then one `vw-motion-shot` helper per shot, three or four at once, given only the shot id; each builds, uploads, checks and snapshots on the server and answers with its last upload's sha256 (with no pictures it stops at a still key frame first). Snapshot each shot at its beats with crops of the parts its rules name (`vw motion snapshot --shot S --at … --crop …`), then a fresh `vw-motion-check` helper per shot with the round number, and `vw motion verdict --shot S --file work/motion/S/check-N.json`. Failed rules go to a new `vw-motion-shot` helper with only those rules; at most two redo rounds, then show the operator the open rules. Put `scene_motion: {sha256, labels, cues}` on the shot (labels word for word; cues `{selector: "#id", word or at_s}`), propose the revision, then `vw motion render --shot S` (free; it checks the timing). It is selected like a take; a drawing without a clean verdict of its project is held. A correction the operator makes that holds for the subject: `vw motion rule --subject … --add "…" --quote "…"`.

stages.name: assembly
steps: First the editor's package (design/115, design/132): once every gap is recorded, `vw delivery bundle` (the narration, the camera cuts by name and time, the raw AI files, the timeline, the EDL, the captions, the cut list and the relink list). The server refuses the assembly without it, and again after a gap is recorded anew: run it again. On the operator's computer (Windows or Mac): `vw pull <code>`, `vw delivery check`, `vw delivery download` (no camera copies by default), then `vw delivery open --originals "<folder>"` on Resolve Studio. Then the assembly below, the proof copy.

`vw assembly prepare`: it lists every gap fill on one line (slot frames, what the take or asset covers, the default: trim from frame 0, or hold the last frame when the take is short; issues such as untagged colour or rotation) and the shots the logs flagged as shaky.

Show the operator that table and ask once: any fill to change (start offset, trim or hold), any flagged shot to stabilise with FFmpeg (counted in the zoom cap), and for each fill with an issue whether to use it as it is or swap it in visuals. Record only the exceptions: `vw assembly choose --shot S --offset f --end trim|hold_last [--accept-as-is]`, or several in out/fills.json with `--file out/fills.json`; `vw assembly stabilize --sub X --choice ffmpeg`. The defaults need no command.

`vw assembly build`, `vw assembly render` (A1 narration with one measured gain, A2 nat sound at the blueprint band, a -3 dBTP ceiling on the mix, no music), `vw assembly status --wait 900` until the film is ready, `vw assembly fetch` (it prints the loudness against the targets). The operator watches AND listens.

On their yes (it must say watched and listened): `vw assembly record --quote "<their words>"` records the review and the output together. On changes: `vw assembly review --decision changes --notes "…" [--frame-note mm:ss:note] --quote "…"`, change the choices the notes name, build and render again (only the changed fills are re-encoded). On a no: `--decision rejected` and `vw revise --stage visuals` or `--stage master` as the notes say.

stages.name: delivery
steps: `vw delivery bundle` again writes the full package with the approved film (approved film, narration, originals used, normalised fills, plans, SRT, finishing checklist, media-pool CSV, OPEN-EDIT).

On the operator's computer (Windows or Mac): `vw pull <code>`, then `vw delivery check` (is Resolve installed, Studio or free, which version, enough disk; the download does not start without it), `vw delivery download` (the whole edit into runs/<code>/edit/, three files at a time, then counted and cross-checked: every file's size and fingerprint, the voiceover byte-identical, every cut pointing at a present file, the timeline's length and cut count equal to the film; the timeline is then written with this computer's paths), `vw delivery open` (free Resolve: three steps, File > Import > Timeline, then the operator plays the start, the middle and the end next to Approved-film.mp4; on their yes `vw delivery confirm --quote "<their words>"`; Resolve Studio, running with external scripting on: `vw delivery open` imports the timeline, exports .drp and .drt into Timeline/ and reads it back at 0 frames), then `vw delivery zip` for the editor. When the camera files are copies, before the handover: `vw delivery relink-check --originals "<folder>"` compares each original with Relink-list.csv and says per file: relinks as is, renamed (the relinked timeline points at the real name), a corrected timeline written (timecode), line up by hand (cuts listed with frame grabs), two originals fit (the operator picks), or no original found. `vw delivery resolve --run` is replaced; never run it (design/107).

Back on the build machine: ask the five questions (watched the film, listened, read the subtitles, the timeline matched the film, package complete) and `vw delivery final --quote "<their words>"`. Then `vw close` (retention: final film and package, narration, approved visuals, records; everything else deleted).
